content:
Yesterday we began to gather the hidden lessons of the manna. We saw it as something to wonder at, something hidden beneath the dew, revealed only by the light of Christ, small like a seed yet full of life, and pure and white like the promises of Yahweh. Today we continue, and we begin with its taste.

The manna was sweet. Exodus 16:31 says, "It tasted like honey wafers.
Yahweh gave Israel food with a pleasant sweetness, and this reminds us of the joy found in the Word of Yahweh. David said, "How sweet your words taste to me; they are sweeter than honey" (Psalm 119:103). Jeremiah said, "When I discovered your words, I devoured them. They are my joy and my heart's delight" (Jeremiah 15:16). To those who love Yahweh, His words are not a burden. They bring comfort to the sorrowful, direction to the confused, hope to the discouraged, and strength to the weak. Sometimes the Word corrects us, and correction may be painful. Yet even correction is sweet when we understand that it comes from a loving Father who desires to lead us toward life.

Numbers 11:8 gives us one more taste, saying the manna "tasted like pastries baked with olive oil". In the Scripture, oil is also connected with Yahweh's Holy Spirit and His anointing. The Scriptures did not come merely from the imagination of men. Second Peter 1:21 says, "Those prophets were moved by the Holy Spirit, and they spoke from God". The words were written through men, but their true source was Yahweh. So, when we receive the Word rightly, we receive both the sweetness of the honey and the richness of the oil; the truth brings joy, but it also carries the power and guidance of Yahweh's Spirit.

We must never separate the Word from the Spirit who inspired it, and we must never claim to follow the Spirit while rejecting the written Word. The Spirit and the Word always work together.

But the manna, though it lay all around the camp, still had to be gathered. Exodus 16:16 says, "Each family should gather as much as it needs". The manna did not float into their tents by itself. It lay upon the ground, but the people had to rise, go out, bend down, and collect it. In the same way, the truth is available in the Scriptures, but we must make the effort to gather it. Having a Bible in our house is not enough. Listening to others speak about Scripture is not enough. Remembering what we learned many years ago is not enough. We must personally search, read, meditate, and gather the truth for ourselves. The person who stayed inside the tent received nothing, even though manna surrounded the whole camp. Likewise, a person may live among believers, attend meetings, and own many Bibles, yet remain spiritually hungry because they never gather the Word for themselves.

And once gathered, the manna had to be prepared. Numbers 11:8 says the people "made flour by grinding it with hand mills or pounding it in mortars. Then they boiled it in a pot and made it into flat cakes". This teaches us to study and carefully arrange the truths of Scripture, for one isolated verse may not reveal the full plan of Yahweh. We must gather all the relevant passages and compare them together. Isaiah 28:10 says Yahweh teaches "one line at a time, one line at a time, a little here, and a little there". One verse gives one part, another adds another part, a prophecy gives the promise, a historical event gives the picture, the teachings of Christ give the explanation, and the apostles help us understand the fulfilment. This does not mean forcing unrelated verses together. It means allowing Scripture to explain Scripture, until, like manna ground into meal and prepared as a complete food, the truth can be understood and spiritually eaten.

The manna also had to be gathered every day, except on the Sabbath, and it had to be gathered early, for Exodus 16:21 says, "After this the flakes melted in the hot sun". In the same way, we need the Word of Yahweh every day. Christ taught his disciples to pray, "Give us today the food we need" (Matthew 6:11). Yesterday's study may have strengthened us yesterday, but today brings new responsibilities, new temptations, new trials, and new decisions. So we need fresh meditation every day. The manna may be available, but it must be collected. The verse may be before us, but it must be studied. The promise may be written, but it must be believed. The command may be clear, but it must be obeyed. We must develop the habit of meeting Yahweh through His Word every single day. And we must remember that this bread came from heaven. No farmer produced it. No human being invented it. Exodus 16:4 says, "Look, I'm going to rain down food from heaven for you". In the same way, the truth of Yahweh does not originate in human wisdom. James 1:17 says, "Whatever is good and perfect is a gift coming down to us from God our Father". Every truth we understand is not a reason for pride. It is a gift from Yahweh.

There is one more thing to notice. The manna lay all around the camp of Israel. Wherever the people looked in the morning, Yahweh's provision was there. Today, the bread of truth is available within the camp of the New Creation, and those who rise, search, and gather can be fed by Yahweh's Word. But this also points toward something much greater. Habakkuk 2:14 says, "For as the waters fill the sea, the earth will be filled with an awareness of the glory of the LORD". Today many people still remain in darkness. Many do not yet know Yahweh's plan, His character, His Kingdom, or the purpose of His salvation. But the day is coming when the knowledge of Yahweh will cover the whole earth. The truth that now nourishes a little flock will one day be made known to all nations. What now covers the camp will one day cover the earth. What is now gathered by a few will one day be offered to all. What a wonderful morning that will be, when the whole world awakens to the knowledge of Yahweh, and the bread of heaven is available for every willing heart to gather.

So let us take these lessons to heart. Let us approach Yahweh's Word with wonder and humility, asking, "What is it?" Let us look beneath the surface and search for the hidden truth. Let us allow the light of Christ to open the Scriptures. Let us value even the smallest seed of the Word. Let us taste its sweetness like honey and receive the richness of the oil of His Spirit. Let us gather all the verses, compare them, and understand Yahweh's complete plan. And let us gather the Word every day while the opportunity is before us, remembering that it came from heaven as a gift from Yahweh Himself. The manna lay around the camp, but only those who went out and gathered it were fed. Therefore let us not remain inside our tents. Let us rise early. Let us bend down humbly. Let us search carefully. Let us gather the hidden manna, and eat until our hearts are strengthened for the whole wilderness journey.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our God,

We thank You that Your words are sweeter than honey and richer than the finest oil.

Teach us not to leave the bread lying on the ground, but to rise and gather it ourselves. Help us to grind and compare Your truths until Your whole plan becomes clear to us. Give us fresh bread every morning, for yesterday's portion cannot feed today's need.

And we long for the day when the knowledge of Your glory will cover the whole earth.

"People do not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God." - Matthew 4:4

In the name of Christ, the true bread from heaven, we pray. Amen.
